name: 2022-23 Makeup - PHY-1071  Engineering Physics
subject: Engineering Physics

questions.markdown: Obtain an expression for the radius of $m$th order bright ring in the case of Newton's rings.

A helium-neon laser having a wavelength of 633 nm delivers $2.00 \times 10^{18}$ photon/s. (i) What is the energy of a photon in eV? (ii) If the beam shines perpendicularly onto a perfectly reflecting surface, what force does it exert on the surface?
The quantum number $n$ of a particle of mass $m$ confined to a one-dimensional "box" of length $L$, when its momentum is $4h/L$ is 4. Is the above statement true /false? Justify.

With necessary diagram, derive an expression for angle of acceptance and numerical aperture for an optical fibre with refractive index of the material of the core $n_1$ and cladding $n_2$ placed in a surrounding medium of refractive index $n_0$.

15.0 mW Helium-Neon laser emits a beam of circular cross section with a diameter of 2.00 mm. (i) Find the maximum electric field in the beam. (ii) What total energy is contained in a 1.00 m length of the beam?
The particle like an electron in an infinite potential well, can be at rest with its energy $E=0$. State True or False and justify your answer.
Derive the Compton shift equation for electromagnetic radiation like x-rays interacting with a free or a nearly free electron.

Electrons are ejected from a metallic surface with speeds of up to $4.60 \times 10^5$ m/s when light with a wavelength of 625 nm is used. (i) What is the work function of the surface? (ii) What is the cut-off frequency for this surface?
In the photoelectric effect, explain why the stopping potential depends on the frequency of light but not on the intensity.
Sketch schematically the plots of Fermi-Dirac distribution function for zero kelvin and for temperature above zero kelvin. Derive an expression for density-of-states.
Explain briefly the BCS theory of superconductivity in metals. Why all conductors are not superconductors?

For copper at 300 K, calculate the probability that a state with an energy equal to 99.0% of the Fermi energy is occupied. Fermi energy of copper is 7.05 eV. Mass of an electron is $9.1\times10^{-31}$ kg; speed of light in vacuum = $3\times10^8$ m/s; Planck's constant = $6.63\times10^{-34}$ Js; Avagadro number = $6.023\times10^{23}$/mol; Boltzmann constant = $1.38\times10^{-23}$ J/K.
